pages.title: Home
pages.seoTitle: Facial & Cosmetic Surgery Westlake TX | Stone Surgical Arts
pages.seoDescription: Boutique facial and cosmetic surgery in Westlake, Texas. Dr. Mona Stone plans and performs every case herself: face, neck and jawline, skin and non-surgical.

props.text: A boutique practice where one surgeon plans your result, performs it, and sees you through every stage after.
Based in Westlake and caring for patients across Southlake, Grapevine, Colleyville, Keller and Fort Worth.
Surgeon, from consult to final follow-up
Four ways into the same idea: a face read as a whole, and a plan that respects how it will look in ten years, not only next month.
Facial plastic surgery for refined, natural results.
Advanced skin rejuvenation for a radiant glow.
Enhance your look with minimal downtime.
A surgeon's training. An artist's eye.

Dr. Stone came to surgery through engineering, and it shows in how she plans: in three dimensions, in structure before skin, and against your own measurements rather than a template. The plan you leave with is hers, and so is every appointment after it.
Biomedical engineering degree, then a Doctorate of Dental Surgery
Full oral and maxillofacial residency across three Level 1 trauma centres
Attending surgeon, Baylor and Methodist Medical Centers
KLS Martin IPS® certified for patient-specific implant planning
Three steps, and no surprises in any of them.
An hour with Dr. Stone, not with a coordinator. You leave knowing what is possible, what is not, and what each option costs.
A written plan with the technique, the recovery and the fee set out. Financing through Sunbit if you want to spread it.
Your procedure, then follow-up with the same surgeon, through the swelling, the settling and the year it takes to look like you always did.
She is asked about this work, not only for it.

Cofounder of a national PPE drive, an attending surgeon at two medical centres, and the person local newsrooms call when the subject is faces. The list is short because it is only what the practice itself published.
Daylight saving and sleep: mitigating the lost hour
Cofounder: PPE for medical professionals during COVID-19
Alumni pitch in to the COVID-19 effort
She said we would start small and work our way up. I am in love with my lips. Plump but natural.

Dr. Stone will hear your concerns and give you all of your options. At no point will you feel pressured in your treatment choices. I started out with more of a conservative maintenance with my cosmetic facial routine and I couldn't be happier with the results.
Dr. Stone and her staff made me feel comfortable and welcomed. My eyelid surgery went very well and I am very pleased. I highly recommend her!
Dr. Stone is so kind and also a great, proactive surgeon. Not only do I send patients to her, I am one myself. The office and staff are equally fantastic.

Absolutely beautiful office with cutting-edge equipment. The staff at Stone Surgical Arts are an amazing team. Dr. Stone is an incredible surgeon, she takes the time to talk through procedures and treatment plans with her patients.

Four months ago I took my daughter to Dr. Stone with her face covered with acne, and through the past few months she has helped my daughter clear her skin tremendously. It's a friendly environment and she's the sweetest doctor ever.
The work speaks in pairs of photographs.
Neck lifts, blepharoplasty, chin and jawline work, fillers and resurfacing, filtered by treatment so you can look only at the one you came for.
Cases are published only with the patient's current written consent, so the gallery fills as the practice's own photography is shot and cleared.
Credit that banks instead of expiring.

Aesthetic care is rarely one appointment. A membership turns a monthly amount into credit that accumulates until you want it: a syringe this spring, or a surgical fee next year, with member pricing on everything in between.
The five questions we are asked most.
What does the consultation cost, and what happens in it?

$175 for Texas residents and $250 from out of state, with a $100 deposit to hold the appointment that comes off the fee. You spend the hour with Dr. Stone rather than a treatment coordinator, and you leave with the options, the honest limits of each, and what each one costs.
How much time will I need away from work?

The practice's own guidance: about a week after eyelid surgery, about ten days after CO2 laser resurfacing, and two weeks after a facelift. Plan for one to two weeks of private time and come back early if recovery goes better than expected. It is always easier that way round than the reverse.

, CareCredit and Scratchpay, and is a preferred provider with all major dental and medical carriers where a procedure is covered. A membership is the other route: it banks credit month by month rather than borrowing against it.
Will I need someone to drive me home?

For anything under intravenous sedation, yes. A responsible adult has to bring you, stay in the office through the procedure and drive you home, and you should not drive or operate machinery for 24 hours afterwards. Treatments done under local anaesthetic alone do not require it.
When can I wear makeup again?
In most cases 48 hours after sutures come out. After CO2 laser, about ten days. Sun avoidance matters more than makeup does in that window: sun on healing skin is what darkens a scar.
One practice in Westlake, serving the north side of the Metroplex.
Personalised care, advanced technique and beautiful, natural results, planned by the surgeon who performs them.

pages.title: Neck Lift
pages.seoTitle: Neck Lift Westlake TX | Stone Surgical Arts
pages.seoDescription: The full surgical procedure, with muscle repair and skin removal, for a neck that has gone past what a suture can hold. $11,000 in Westlake, TX.

props.text: The full surgical procedure, with muscle repair and skin removal, for a neck that has gone past what a suture can hold.
$18,000 with the face, planned and performed together
A neck lift is not a skin operation.
Three layers have changed and a result that lasts means addressing all three in the same sitting. The one people expect to hear about is the one nearest the surface, and it is the least of them.
The sheet of muscle that gives the neck its shape, repaired where it has separated. This is the layer that holds, and it is the reason a neck lift lasts longer than anything that only tightens skin.
Where the muscle is lax but the skin still has tone, a suture suspension may be enough on its own. That is the MyEllevate
conversation, and it is a cheaper and shorter one.
Contoured where it has accumulated under the chin and along the jaw, so that the border the muscle repair creates has a clean line to sit against rather than a soft one.
Fullness under the chin is sometimes fat rather than muscle, and sometimes both. Which it is on you is measured at the consultation, not guessed at from a photograph.
Removed where it is genuinely in excess, rather than redraped over the problem. Treating the skin as the problem is how a neck ends up looking operated on rather than rested.
Skin is the last layer and the one everybody names first. A procedure that only pulls it tight is why work that has been done looks done.
The test is whether the skin takes up when you lift your chin.
This is the operation when there is real skin excess. If the skin retracts when the chin is raised, a suspension procedure may still be enough. If it hangs, it needs removing.
Which of these sound like you?
Loose skin that does not take up when the chin is raised
Vertical banding down the front of the neck, visible at rest as well as when speaking
A jawline that has lost its border entirely rather than softened
Significant weight loss that has left the neck with more skin than it needs
Tick whichever apply. Nothing here is stored or sent.
Where the skin still has tone and the problem is muscle laxity, MyEllevate
achieves a great deal at $6,000 with no external incision and a far shorter recovery. Dr. Stone will recommend the smaller operation where it will do the job.
Under the chin, then around and behind the ears.

A small incision under the chin gives access to the platysma, which is repaired in the midline where it has separated. Fat is contoured through the same opening. Incisions around and behind the ears follow the natural creases and are where the skin is redraped and the excess removed.
Scars are placed where the anatomy conceals them and they mature over months from pink to pale. Scar care starts as soon as the wounds are closed and is part of the plan rather than an afterthought.
A drain is used sometimes, for the first day or two, depending on how much work the neck needed. If one is used it comes out at the first post-operative visit.
A day, a fortnight, and six months of settling.
The figures below are the practice's conventional ranges and they are what you should plan around. Dr. Stone will give you the numbers for your own neck at the consultation.
Two to four hours in theatre
Under general anaesthetic or deep sedation. A responsible adult brings you, waits, and drives you home. You do not drive yourself for this one, and you should not for twenty-four hours afterwards.
A support garment, swelling and tightness. Day three is the worst of it and it improves quickly after that, which is worth knowing in advance rather than discovering.
Sutures out, back at a desk

Sutures come out in stages across the first two weeks. Most people are back at a desk at two weeks and comfortable in company shortly after. Plan for the fortnight and come back early if it goes well.
The result keeps refining as swelling resolves and the tissues soften. Follow-ups are with Dr. Stone, not with a nurse you have not met.
The first fortnight is at home.
By month three most people have stopped thinking about it.
Three operations, and what decides between them.
Which of these you need is an anatomical fact rather than a preference. None of them is sold as a package beforehand and all three are quoted separately.
Neck and jawline procedures compared. Fees are the practice's own.
Muscle laxity, where the skin still has tone
Muscle separation, fat and genuine skin excess
The jowl and the neck, where they are one continuous problem
Under the chin, around and behind the ears
In front of and behind the ears, back into the hairline
A jawline implant is the fourth conversation and a different one: it adds projection to a mandible that never had it, which no amount of lifting will create. $10,000.
The nerve that moves your lower lip runs through this operation.

The marginal mandibular nerve runs exactly where a neck lift works. A surgeon has to know that anatomy in three dimensions, in a particular neck, under tension, rather than as a diagram. Dr. Stone spent her residency rebuilding it after it had been broken, which is the background she brings to an elective neck.
Biomedical engineering degree, then a Doctorate of Dental Surgery
Full oral and maxillofacial residency across three Level 1 trauma centres
Attending surgeon, Baylor and Methodist Medical Centers
She plans, performs and follows up every case herself
The six questions this operation raises.
How is this different from MyEllevate

suspends the platysma with a suture and removes nothing, so there is no external incision and the recovery is days rather than weeks. A neck lift removes skin and repairs muscle directly. The first is for laxity, the second for excess, and which you have is an anatomical fact rather than a preference.
A small incision under the chin, and incisions around and behind the ears following the natural creases. They are placed where the anatomy conceals them and they mature over months from pink to pale.
The practice puts a full surgical neck lift at up to ten years, against about five for MyEllevate
. The muscle repair is durable; what changes is that your neck keeps ageing around it. Skin quality, weight stability and genetics all move that number.
Sometimes, for the first day or two, depending on how much work the neck needed. If one is used it is removed at your first post-operative visit and it is a great deal less unpleasant than it sounds.

You and Dr. Stone go through your concerns and your goals, she takes a medical history and assesses your general health, and photographs and measurements are taken so the plan is drawn against your own anatomy. You leave knowing whether this is the right procedure for you, and if it is not, which one is.
What does it cost, and can I finance it?
$11,000 for the neck alone, or $18,000 combined with the face. Financing runs through
, and membership credit can be applied to a surgical fee.
One surgeon, from the consultation to the last follow-up.

The consultation is $175 for Texas residents and $250 from out of state, with a $100 deposit that comes off the fee. You spend the hour with Dr. Stone rather than with a treatment coordinator, and you leave knowing whether this is the right operation for you.
